summary.text: A 58-year-old man was admitted after falling on the bathroom floor with a severe right-hand injury and right leg pain. His history included hypertension, prostate cancer, hepatitis C infection, heart failure, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, an ascending thoracic aorta aneurysm, severe bilateral knee osteoarthritis and a right total knee replacement 10 years earlier. He was febrile and hypotensive, with a swollen right knee and an infected open finger wound.

CT showed right knee joint deformation and effusion without signs of osteomyelitis, and orthopedic surgery judged surgery not indicated. Vancomycin, cefepime, metronidazole and fluids were started on admission. On day 3 blood cultures grew MRSA and six weeks of intravenous antibiotics were planned for presumed hardware infection or septic arthritis. The regimen changed to daptomycin and was switched back to vancomycin on day 5.

On day 11 he developed hematuria and generalized body pain; examination showed scleral icterus, abdominal tenderness and agitation. Hemoglobin dropped sharply, indirect bilirubin and creatinine were elevated, haptoglobin was low, the direct Coombs test was positive and the smear showed schistocytes and other abnormal cells. Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia was considered, prednisone did not help, and on day 13 vancomycin was switched to ceftaroline.

The hemoglobin nadir was 4.2 g/dL, and he received 2 units of pRBC, methylprednisolone with a taper, and intravenous immunoglobin. Vancomycin-dependent RBC antibodies were detected and confirmed vancomycin-induced hemolytic anemia. Hemoglobin stabilized and he was discharged on day 30.
